citations.quote: Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

Let a balanced sutured manifold be taut. For a specified coherent orientation class, its integral sutured Floer homology has a direct summand isomorphic to the integers. More precisely, a finite good taut hierarchy terminating in product balls induces a split inclusion of the terminal product homology into the original homology, with orientation classes induced along the cuts.

Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and let $(M,\gamma)$ be the balanced sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact exterior of $K$ along $F$. For a surface-adapted admissible sutured Heegaard diagram, the generator correspondence between the top Alexander summand of the knot Floer complex and the sutured Floer disk-count module identifies their disk-count differentials. Under the hypotheses of a horizontal decomposition, the induced chain map realizes Ni's horizontal decomposition formula. Under the hypotheses of a separating product annulus with connected $R_+$ and $R_-$, the induced chain map realizes Ni's product-annulus tensor formula. These assertions use the specified basepoint domains, periodic-domain admissibility, and exact characteristic-product-region hypotheses; they make no claim that generic Heegaard disk existence alone supplies the decomposition maps.

For the actual marked Seifert surface of genus g, oriented as minus the fiber for the cut, an adapted generator x has Alexander degree g minus the number of its interior polygon coordinates. Thus the top degree-g generators are exactly the outer generators and correspond to the cut diagram generators with their ordered intersection signs. If the integral top homology is one copy of the integers, the actual cut incidence matrix is unimodular, the cut is an integral homology product, and its periodic-domain group vanishes.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, define

$$\mathcal G(K):=\{n\in\mathbb N_0: \text{there is a Seifert surface }F\text{ for }K\text{ with }g(F)=n\}.$$

Every element of $\mathcal G(K)$ is the genus of a connected compact oriented surface. The existence theorem makes $\mathcal G(K)$ nonempty, and the well-ordering of $\mathbb N_0$ gives its least element. The **smooth knot genus** is $g(K):=\min\mathcal G(K)$. This genus is the minimum over embedded spanning surfaces; it is not the number of Seifert circles or the genus of every surface produced from a diagram.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a finite collection of admitted compact marked sutured diagrams, a finite sequence of diagram moves or surface cuts, and finite-dimensional parameter families of dimension at most two. Suppose the local Fredholm, finite-dimensional Sard, compactness and gluing constructions are supplied for their actual Cauchy–Riemann operators, including the prescribed endpoint and protected-neighborhood conditions. All selections needed to apply those constructions, choose coherent determinant orientations, and obtain simultaneous regular data can then be made under Countable Choice. In particular no uncountable choice of analytic charts or regular data is needed for these fixed finite integral Floer constructions.

derivations.claim: Choose a Seifert surface F realizing the least genus g=g(K), and let E be the compact exterior. The exterior is irreducible: a sphere in its interior bounds two balls in S³ by F1; the connected knot neighborhood lies entirely on one side, so the other ball is disjoint from it and lies in E. A small oriented meridian loop meets F once, so F is nonseparating: a separating two-sided surface would have algebraic intersection zero with every closed loop. Cut E along the connected F to obtain connected M with the product annular suture and the two F faces. Their Euler characteristics agree and the boundary meets that suture, so M is balanced. A sphere in M is disjoint from F in E. Its E-ball is also disjoint from F: since F is connected, disjoint from the sphere, and has its boundary on ∂E outside that interior ball, it lies entirely on the other side. Thus that ball remains a ball in M. This proves irreducibility of the actual cut without a general-Y irreducibility assertion.

The two faces are incompressible. A compression of F along a nonseparating essential circle produces a connected Seifert surface of genus g−1. A separating compression produces a boundary-bearing Seifert component and a closed component. The latter has positive genus, since otherwise the original compression circle bounded a disk on F; discarding it again gives a Seifert surface of genus strictly less than g. Both contradict minimality. A face compression in M would be such a compression in E. For g=0 the disk has no essential compression circle.

To prove the actual sutured norm-minimality, take any compact oriented properly embedded competitor T representing the positive face class in H₂(M,γ;Z). Its total oriented boundary in H₁(γ;Z) is one copy of the longitude. Put its boundary circles in the interior of the annular suture. Cap an innermost contractible boundary circle by its disk in the annulus, pushed into the boundary collar; this operation increases Euler characteristic and cannot increase the Thurston complexity. Continue until every boundary circle is essential. Whenever both orientations remain, choose an adjacent opposite pair. The annulus between them contains no other boundary circle. Glue it to T in a thin boundary collar and round the corners. This gives an embedded oriented surface and removes the pair. Euler characteristic is unchanged; if two components merge, the inequality max(0,−(χ₁+χ₂))≤max(0,−χ₁)+max(0,−χ₂) shows that total complexity cannot increase. For two circles on one component its Euler characteristic, hence complexity, is unchanged. The finite sequence ends with exactly one essential boundary circle, since its total winding is one. Delete all closed components, which also cannot increase complexity. The remaining connected surface embeds in E and extends across the knot collar to an actual Seifert surface for K of the same genus. Its genus is at least g by minimality. For g≥1 its complexity is therefore at least 2g−1=x(F); for g=0 it is at least zero=x(F). It follows that x(T)≥x(F). The same argument applies to the negative face. Thus M is the actual taut balanced sutured manifold, by irreducibility and norm-minimality. The boundary cancellations were used only to derive a lower bound and need not preserve the competitor's relative class after it is mapped to E.

Apply the restricted branch F6 to the fixed finite hierarchy and its diagram choices: the integer domain classes, required finite parameter families, separable Sobolev/perturbation spaces and protected neighborhoods are exactly the inputs described there. This makes the simultaneous regular data, compactness extractions, gluing charts and determinant selections under Countable Choice. With these choices, apply the actual construction F3 to the marked Seifert surface F. Its meridional frame, rather than an unspecified closure framing, gives an admissible adapted representative. By F4 every generator has Alexander degree g−n_P(x), with n_P(x) a nonnegative integer. Hence its whole integral chain complex has no generator, and thus no homology, in a grading greater than g.

The entire degree-g summand is the outer summand, and F3 identifies its signed differential with the actual cut complex of M. Since M is taut, F2 gives that this cut homology contains a split copy of Z for the orientation class induced by the given knot complex. Consequently the integral knot Floer group at degree g is nonzero. This also covers g=0: the taut cut argument and the same signed chain map apply to the minimum disk, without a genus-one connected-sum or field-coefficient substitution.

Degree g is nonzero and every larger degree is zero, so the maximum of the stated nonvanishing degree set is exactly g(K). The proof uses only the literal S³ ball-side and minimum-Seifert-genus arguments above; it makes no claim of arbitrary general-Y Thurston norm detection.

citations.quote: An actual good decomposing surface admits an adapted admissible nice diagram. For a specified coherent orientation class on the exterior complex, the outer summand of that diagram is integrally chain isomorphic to the cut diagram with the induced orientation class; nonzero periodic domains are retained by pullback of characters. When the surface separates into two balanced pieces, every generator is outer and the full complex is identified with the graded tensor product of the two component complexes. In particular the usual two-piece horizontal decomposition has this chain formula. It gives the homology tensor formula over every field; over the integers it gives the graded Künneth exact sequence including Tor.

Let a balanced sutured manifold have connected positive and negative boundary faces. An essential separating product-annulus decomposition into balanced pieces admits a graded integral tensor chain equivalence, with coherent orientation classes induced from the specified class. This realizes the homology tensor formula over every field and the integral Künneth formula with Tor. Product-disk decompositions and product one-handle additions have literal integral complex identifications. The closure construction for any connected pair of faces identifies its top knot complex with the actual sutured disk complex using the specified marking and orientation class.

Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold, let $K\subset Y$ be a smooth oriented null-homologous knot, and let $F\subset Y$ be a compact connected oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $K$. Choose a closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, put $M=Y\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, and let $\gamma_\mu$ be the union of two disjoint annuli on $\partial M$ whose core sutures are parallel meridians of $K$ with opposite orientations. Delete a collar of $\partial F$ to regard $F$ as a properly embedded surface in $(M,\gamma_\mu)$, with relative class $[F]\in H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb Z)$. Let $t_\mu$ be the meridional boundary trivialization of the oriented plane field used in the relative Spin-c definition. For $\mathfrak{s}\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(M,\gamma_\mu)$, its Alexander grading is

$$A_F(\mathfrak{s})=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak{s},t_\mu),[F]\right\rangle,$$

with the standard sign convention that gives the usual Alexander grading for knots in $S^3$. For a balanced admissible sutured Heegaard diagram of $(M,\gamma_\mu)$, the Spin-c summand $SFH(M,\gamma_\mu,\mathfrak{s};\mathbb Z)$ is the homology of the integral sutured Floer disk-count complex generated by the Heegaard generators assigned to $\mathfrak{s}$. Define the integral knot Floer group in Alexander grading $i$ by

$$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],i;\mathbb Z)=\bigoplus_{\substack{\mathfrak{s}\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(M,\gamma_\mu)\\ A_F(\mathfrak{s})=i}}SFH(M,\gamma_\mu,\mathfrak{s};\mathbb Z).$$

This fixes the integral coefficient convention. The equivalent associated-graded closed Heegaard-complex presentation, invariance under changing diagrams, and comparison with the mod-two grid complex are separate theorems; this definition supplies none of their proofs or a coefficient-change map.

For the actual marked Seifert surface of genus g, oriented as minus the fiber for the cut, an adapted generator x has Alexander degree g minus the number of its interior polygon coordinates. Thus the top degree-g generators are exactly the outer generators and correspond to the cut diagram generators with their ordered intersection signs. If the integral top homology is one copy of the integers, the actual cut incidence matrix is unimodular, the cut is an integral homology product, and its periodic-domain group vanishes.

derivations.claim: Construct the actual marked closure/adapted surface diagram from the relative Morse handles, carrying the page longitude and meridional boundary frame. Positive boundary fingers, the uniform relative windings, and permissible niceification give the admitted diagram. The Chern obstruction formula evaluates on minus F as minus 2g plus twice the number of interior polygon coordinates. Consequently its degree-g generators are exactly its outer generators. Each index-one disk is an exhausted embedded bigon or rectangle and lifts uniquely in the cut/double surface. The literal Fredholm conjugacies and the pullback of the specified periodic-domain orientation character align every coefficient after generator signs. Thus this generator correspondence identifies the full disk-count differentials over the integers. Signed relative moves transport the identification to the defining complexes, with their markings and coherent orientation classes.

For a horizontal decomposition, the cut components are balanced. In its adapted diagram there is no reverse cross-family intersection from side two to side one; the equal row and column counts force every perfect-matching generator to avoid the polygon. Thus the whole complex is the outer complex. The cut surface is a disjoint union, so each index-one disk has exactly one nonconstant factor. Ordering determinant factors gives the Koszul differential ∂(x1⊗x2)=∂x1⊗x2+(−1)^|x1|x1⊗∂x2. This is the horizontal chain map and the complete integral chain formula. Taking homology over any field gives Ni's horizontal formula. Taking homology over the integers instead gives the Künneth exact sequence including Tor; no unqualified integral homology tensor formula is asserted.

For an essential separating product annulus with connected R+ and R−, form the two rounded horizontal surfaces from opposite boundary faces and the annulus. Their actual cobordism regions give the required relative class and their Euler sums give the horizontal equality. This reduces the operation to attachment of a product region. A rooted cut-arc forest removes a product region meeting the sutures by literal product-disk identifications. For an interior essential product region, the explicit once-punctured-torus block forces its two fixed coordinates and isolates the only possible extra genus-one two-corner domain, whose Maslov index is minus one; it cannot contribute. Both comparison diagrams therefore have precisely the same supported disks and conjugate oriented operators in the unchanged complement. The resulting integral chain identification, followed by the remaining product-disk cuts, gives the full separating-annulus graded tensor operation. It gives Ni's field formula and the integral Künneth/Tor formulation as above. All constructions keep the stated basepoint zero regions, actual periodic lattices and essential-annulus hypotheses. They apply when the specified characteristic product region supplies those actual surfaces; they do not infer its geometry from generic disk existence.

derivations.claim: Let $E$ be the compact exterior and $(M,\gamma)$ its cut along $F$. Its two faces are copies of $F$, and its vertical boundary is the annulus $\partial F\times I$. It is balanced: both faces have Euler characteristic $1-2g$, no component is closed, and every boundary component meets the vertical annulus. A meridian intersects $F$ algebraically once, so $F$ is nonseparating and the cut is connected.

The irreducibility assumption applies to $E$: pushing away the deleted-knot end identifies every compact sphere question with that in $Y\setminus K$. A sphere in the interior of $M$ is therefore a sphere disjoint from $F$ in $E$ and bounds a ball in $E$. Since $F$ is connected and disjoint from this sphere, if it entered the ball it would lie wholly in its interior, contradicting $\partial F\subset\partial E$. The ball is consequently disjoint from $F$; shrink the cut collar if necessary to obtain the same ball in $M$. Thus $M$ is irreducible.

The signed cut comparison gives $\operatorname{SFH}(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)\cong\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. The grading uses the supplied class $[F]$ and genus of this actual surface; no genus-detection theorem for a different ambient manifold is substituted.

If $(M,\gamma)$ were not taut, its integral sutured Floer homology would vanish by the external vanishing input, contradicting step 2.1. Therefore it is taut. This is the contrapositive of F2, not a reversal of taut hierarchy nonvanishing.

If the taut balanced $(M,\gamma)$ were not a product, F3 would give $\mathbb Z^2\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SFH}(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)$. Such an injection into $\mathbb Z$ is impossible: images $a,b$ of its two basis vectors satisfy the nontrivial integer relation $b a-a b=0$ when either is nonzero, and an image zero itself contradicts injectivity. The two disjoint outer summands in the source argument therefore contradict step 2.1. Hence the actual $F$-cut exterior is a product sutured manifold. This includes $g=0$ and uses the corrected characteristic-pair qualification F4.

citations.quote: Let a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented three-manifold be fibered with a specified connected oriented Seifert fiber. Its compact exterior with two meridional sutures admits a good surface-adapted balanced diagram carrying that actual Seifert surface, its boundary longitude, and the meridional boundary trivialization. For a fiber of an actual open book the cut/double diagram represents the marked product obtained by cutting along the fiber, with the original monodromy retained in regluing.

A good admissible surface-adapted balanced diagram can be made nice by a finite sequence of permissible fingers and own-family disk slides preserving its surface marking. Weak admissibility is preserved. Every complementary region of the underlying diagram disjoint from its true boundary is a bigon or square.

Two balanced Heegaard diagrams of the same marked sutured manifold are connected by relative attaching-circle isotopies, own-family disk slides, and ordinary stabilizations and destabilizations. An ordinary stabilization can be moved by such slides to the true boundary region. These moves induce integral chain homotopy equivalences for the transported coherent orientation class. The product sutured manifold has integral homology equal to one copy of the integers; on a homology-product branch the periodic-domain character ambiguity vanishes.

For the actual marked Seifert surface of genus g, oriented as minus the fiber for the cut, an adapted generator x has Alexander degree g minus the number of its interior polygon coordinates. Thus the top degree-g generators are exactly the outer generators and correspond to the cut diagram generators with their ordered intersection signs. If the integral top homology is one copy of the integers, the actual cut incidence matrix is unimodular, the cut is an integral homology product, and its periodic-domain group vanishes.

For an actual nice admissible good surface diagram whose cut has zero periodic-domain group, the outer differential and the cut differential are identified over the integers after changing generator signs. This identifies the top Alexander homology with the integral homology of the cut diagram when the surface is the marked Seifert surface and the outer degree is its genus. The conclusion applies in particular to a fiber cut and to the rank-one branch of the cut Euler-matrix reduction.

derivations.claim: Use the actual binding bridge and drilling construction to represent the exterior with two meridional sutures, carrying the actual page longitude and the class of F. The adapted surface cut is literally the result of cutting this mapping torus along its fiber, hence is F times an interval with its product sutures. Apply the finite permissible niceification. Signed relative diagram moves compare the resulting complex to the chosen defining complex, with its specified coherent orientation class transported. No restriction on Y or change of coefficient ring is made.

In this marked adapted diagram the local Euler obstruction is minus 2g plus twice the number of interior polygon coordinates when evaluated on minus F. Therefore the Alexander degree is g minus that number: degree g is precisely the outer generator set, and no higher degree occurs. The product cut has zero periodic-domain group, either directly from its empty product diagram and the relative handle description, or from its vanishing relative integral homology. The signed cut comparison consequently identifies the whole degree-g differential with the cut differential, after harmless changes of generator signs.

The empty diagram of the actual product has one empty-tuple generator and no nonconstant disk, so its integral chain complex is Z with zero differential. The signed relative move equivalences identify its homology with that of the actual cut diagram. Combining with the full top-summand chain identification gives the asserted integral group isomorphism. The exterior orientation character restricts trivially to the zero-periodic cut, so this conclusion holds for the specified defining class without asserting equivalence of arbitrary orientation systems on the uncut exterior.

citations.quote: Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $Y\setminus K$ be irreducible, and let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface. If the integral top Alexander group $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$, then the sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact knot exterior along $F$ is a product sutured manifold. The argument uses Ni's homology-product reduction, the horizontal and separating product-annulus decompositions, the characteristic product region, and Gabai's taut-foliation input under their stated hypotheses.

derivations.claim: Apply F1 to the actual class $[F]$, the actual genus $g$ and the given integral group. The cut exterior is a product $F\times[0,1]$ as a sutured manifold. In particular the two horizontal faces correspond to the two copies of the original $F$, rather than to a surface selected only by a genus or homology calculation.

To restore the exterior, identify those two faces using their actual gluing map. In product coordinates this is $(x,1)\sim(h(x),0)$ for a self-homeomorphism $h:F\to F$. Thus the exterior is the mapping torus of $h$. Its projection to $[0,1]/(0\sim1)=S^1$ is a surface bundle, and the seam is precisely the original embedded $F$.

The vertical boundary is the mapping torus of $\partial F$. Its boundary collar extends this bundle over the deleted-knot end, giving the fibration of $Y\setminus K$ with fiber the interior of $F$, or equivalently with compact fiber $F$ in the compact exterior. This proves the stated fiberedness with the prescribed surface, for arbitrary $Y$ and also for genus zero.

derivations.claim: Both named diagrams are alternating. Apply [F1] with the two polynomials in [F2]. In the trefoil case the coefficients in Alexander degrees $1,0,-1$ have absolute values $1,1,1$, with zero coefficients elsewhere. Thus the maximum nonzero Alexander grading is $1$ and its integral group is $\mathbb Z$. In the $5_2$ case the corresponding absolute values are $2,3,2$, with zero coefficients elsewhere. Its maximum grading is again $1$, with integral top group $\mathbb Z^2$. The formula for the supporting Maslov degree is exactly that of [F1]; no signature sign is guessed from a drawing.

By [F3] the genus is one for both knots. The trefoil's integral top group is $\mathbb Z$, so the fiberedness equivalence in [F3] proves that it is fibered. For $5_2$, $\mathbb Z^2$ is not isomorphic to $\mathbb Z$ (tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ already distinguishes their dimensions), so the same equivalence proves that it is not fibered. These arguments prove every Example clause at its full integral coefficient scope. They do not invoke an unearned generic-$Y$ local supplier or weaken a rank over integers to a mod-two rank.
